lines.en: In 1772, amateur sumo wrestlers in present-day Niigata were performing to raise money for a local temple when a pair of sumo pros crashed their event.
lines.zh: 一七七二年，在今天的新潟，一群业余相扑力士正在表演、为当地一座寺庙募捐，这时两名职业相扑力士闯了进来搅了场子。

lines.en: These wrestlers from the Tokyo sumo guild claimed that only their guild had the right to charge audiences admission.
lines.zh: 这两位来自江户相扑行会的力士声称：只有他们的行会才有权向观众收取入场费。

lines.en: But when the pros tried making off with the ticket money, one was killed and the other barely escaped alive.
lines.zh: 但当这两名职业选手试图卷走票款时，其中一人被打死，另一人差点没能活着逃出去。

lines.en: Back in Tokyo, the guild took their case to a magistrate.
lines.zh: 回到江户，行会把这场官司告到了地方官面前。

lines.en: They argued that because they were the only guild that adhered to sumo’s most “ancient practices,” no other performers in the country were legitimate.
lines.zh: 他们主张：因为只有他们这个行会恪守着相扑最「古老的做法」，全国其他地方的表演者都不算正统。

lines.en: The magistrate accepted this claim.
lines.zh: 地方官采纳了这一说法。

lines.en: But surprisingly, these so-called “ancient practices” were actually recent inventions.
lines.zh: 但出人意料的是，这些所谓的「古老做法」，其实是最近才被发明出来的。

lines.en: So, what were these fabricated traditions, and how do they relate to sumo’s true history?
lines.zh: 那么，这些被编造出来的传统究竟是些什么？它们跟相扑真正的历史又有什么关系？

lines.en: Our earliest reliable records of sumo come from the 8th century, when performances were held as entertainment for annual court banquets.
lines.zh: 关于相扑最早可靠的记载出现在八世纪，那时的表演是作为宫廷年度宴会的助兴节目。

lines.en: During these events, wrestlers were summoned from across Japan as a demonstration of the emperor's influence.
lines.zh: 在这些场合，力士们从日本各地被召集而来，以此彰显天皇的势力。

lines.en: Initially, these wrestlers would punch, scratch, and grab their opponents, claiming victory by forcing their hands or knees to the ground.
lines.zh: 起初，这些力士会挥拳、抓挠、扭抱对手，只要逼得对方的手或者膝盖着地，就算取胜。

lines.en: But eventually, matches began focusing on grappling and tripping techniques.
lines.zh: 但后来，比赛的重心逐渐转到了扭抱和绊摔的技巧上。

lines.en: Over time, power shifted from the emperor and his court to their hired soldiers, the samurai, and official court sumo ended in 1174.
lines.zh: 随着时间推移，权力从天皇和他的宫廷转移到了他们雇来的武士手中，官方的宫廷相扑也在一一七四年宣告终止。

lines.en: However, samurai leaders still had soldiers perform less formal sumo bouts for exercise and entertainment.
lines.zh: 不过，武士的首领们仍然会让手下的士兵进行一些不那么正式的相扑对抗，既是操练，也是消遣。

lines.en: Throughout imperial and samurai rule, sumo was performed across Japan for sport, spectacle, and martial training.
lines.zh: 在整个天皇时代和武士统治期间，相扑在日本各地都有演出，目的各有不同：有竞技，有表演，也有武术训练。

lines.en: But in the 1400s, it took on a new function: fundraising.
lines.zh: 但到了十五世纪，它又增添了一项新功能：筹款。

lines.en: Shrines and temples began hosting performances to raise money for construction and repairs.
lines.zh: 神社和寺院开始主办相扑表演，为建造和修缮筹措经费。

lines.en: And since skilled performers brought in more customers, event promoters were eager to enlist the best wrestlers.
lines.zh: 由于技艺高超的力士能招来更多顾客，各活动的组织者都急于请到最好的力士登场。

lines.en: This led performers to create the first sumo guilds, ensuring steady employment and improving their working conditions.
lines.zh: 这促使表演者们成立了第一批相扑行会，既能保证稳定的工作，也能改善他们的从业条件。

lines.en: Once wrestlers could reliably make money through sumo, they became eager to perform for as many paying customers as possible.
lines.zh: 一旦力士们能靠相扑稳定地挣钱，他们就迫不及待地想为尽可能多的付费观众表演。

lines.en: Enterprising young men put on rowdy street corner sumo performances, hoping to attract the donations of passersby.
lines.zh: 一些有冲劲的年轻人开始在街角搞起喧闹的相扑表演，希望能吸引路人投钱。

lines.en: Lacking the organization of formal performances, these bouts often resulted in fights and injuries among both participants and spectators.
lines.zh: 由于缺少正规演出那样的秩序，这类比拼常常演变成打架，闹得参与者和观众两方都有人受伤。

lines.en: So it didn’t take long for samurai authorities to crack down, periodically banning all forms of sumo in larger cities.
lines.zh: 于是没过多久，武士当局就出手打压，时不时在大城市里禁止一切形式的相扑。

lines.en: Wrestlers and organizers knew they needed to make changes to overcome these bans.
lines.zh: 力士和组织者心里都明白：要破除这些禁令，就必须作出改变。

lines.en: First, they established a boundary to separate spectators from participants.
lines.zh: 首先，他们划出了一道界线，把观众和参加者分开。

lines.en: This boundary took many forms, but over the 17th century it morphed into a standard ring called the dohyō.
lines.zh: 这道界线有过多种形式，但在整个十七世纪里，它逐渐演变成一种标准化的场地，叫作「土俵」。

lines.en: This ring outlined the field of play, introducing a pivotal new rule: now matches could also be won by pushing one’s opponent out of the dohyō.
lines.zh: 这个圈子界定了比赛的范围，也带来了一条关键的新规则：从这时起，比赛还可以靠把对手推出土俵之外来取胜。

lines.en: This innovation increased the advantage of heavier wrestlers, whose weight already helped them topple their opponents.
lines.zh: 这项创新加重了体型较重的力士的优势——他们的体重本来就有助放倒对手。

lines.en: But sumo’s journey to become a respectable sport really took off when promoters began introducing rituals to associate sumo with Japan’s ancient past.
lines.zh: 但相扑真正起步成为一项受人尊敬的体育运动，是在主办者们引入种种仪式、把相扑与日本的古老历史绑在一起之后。

lines.en: Wrestlers threw salt in the ring and rinsed their mouths with water before matches— actions that evoked ancient religious ceremonies.
lines.zh: 力士们往场里撒盐，赛前用水漱口——这些动作让人联想到古代的宗教仪式。

lines.en: These invented traditions imbued the sport with cultural legitimacy, convincing authorities that sumo was above board.
lines.zh: 这些被发明出来的传统，给这项运动注入了文化上的正当性，让当局相信相扑是光明正大的。

lines.en: One notable ritual emerged in 1789, when the Tokyo guild began having their top-ranked wrestlers perform a ring-entering ceremony wearing a sacred rope called the yokozuna.
lines.zh: 一七八九年出现了一项值得一提的仪式：江户的行会开始让级别最高的力士腰系一条叫作「横纲」的神圣绳索，表演入场仪式。

lines.en: This innovation became so popular, the shōgun himself summoned the troupe for a performance— giving legitimacy not just to the Tokyo guild, but specifically to their invented traditions.
lines.zh: 这项创新大受欢迎，连将军本人都把这个班子召去表演——这不仅赋予了江户行会正统地位，更是赋予了他们那些被发明出来的传统以正统地位。

lines.en: After the shogunate was overthrown in 1868, sumo was seen as a dated relic and briefly fell out of fashion.
lines.zh: 一八六八年幕府被推翻之后，相扑被视为过时的遗物，一时之间失了宠。

lines.en: But the sport gradually remade itself for the modern era, and today, Japan holds six 15-day tournaments every year, all of which are broadcast worldwide.
lines.zh: 但这项运动渐渐为现代社会重新塑造了自己。今天，日本每年要举办六场为期十五天的赛事，全部向全世界转播。

lines.en: New technology has brought advantages like instant replays, while other innovations were introduced to evoke the ancient past.
lines.zh: 新技术带来了即时回放这样的好处，而另一些创新，则是为了唤起人们对古老年代的追忆。

lines.en: And over the last century, the average body weight in the upper division has increased by over 60 kilograms!
lines.zh: 而在过去的一百年里，最高级别力士的平均体重增加了六十多公斤！

lines.en: But throughout its changes, sumo has sustained its status as a beloved form of entertainment, a grand display of strength, and an ode to national traditions— both real and invented.
lines.zh: 但在所有这些变迁之中，相扑始终保有着它的地位：一种备受喜爱的娱乐形式、一场力量之美的盛大展示，以及一首献给民族传统的颂歌——无论那些传统是真实的，还是被发明出来的。
